pages.text: "Let's play with everything!" Dari scattered toys on the spiral stairs. Ball on one step, shell on another, then another ball, another shell. Playing was fun; tidying wasn't. Kongal watched from a cradle below.
That evening, Dad climbed to light the lighthouse. A ball rolled beneath him and he stumbled! Gripping the rail, he cried, "That was close!" Toys covered the stairs.
Dari's favorite squeaky fish was missing, too. He looked up and down the steps, but couldn't find it. Tears gathered and his nose stung.
Dad came down and sat beside him. "Why so sad?" Looking around the stairs, he smiled. "Don't worry. I'll teach you some magic."
Dad raised a flipper. "Leave it messy, and feet hurt, the fish hides, and the stairs frown." Dari said, "These stairs are hurting!"
Dad leaned his long muzzle closer. "But tidy up, and feet feel fine, the fish appears, and the stairs smile! That's back-in-place magic." Dari wanted to try.
Dad taught a song. "One, sort by kind! Two, back in place! Three, smile when done!" Balls rolled into their box; shells clattered into their tub. Dari sang, "Back in place!"
At the bottom step, Dari lifted the last ball. Under it—his squeaky fish! He hugged it. Squeak! Dari slapped his tail. "Tidying made it appear!"
Now Dari followed three steps after play. "One, sort by kind! Two, back in place! Three, smile when done!" He squeezed the fish for Kongal, who giggled in the cradle.
Dad sat beside Dari on the bottom step and rested his chin on his back. "Our tidy-up champion!" Clean stairs, comfortable feet, happy heart! Back in place! Every spiral step shone.
